materials.effect: Part snaps under bending or impact load along layer lines
materials.cause: Anisotropic FDM layer bonding weak along Z-axis print direction
materials.action: Reorient print angle by 45-90 deg or increase wall perimeter loops

materials.effect: Corrosion thin-out and localized stress concentration
materials.cause: Uncoated carbon steel exposed to ambient humidity/moisture
materials.action: Specify protective plating (zinc), powder coat, or switch to 304/316SS

materials.effect: Loss of joint clamping force, hinge loosening, or dimensional drift
materials.cause: Continuous compressive loads over time, severely accelerated by operating temperatures above 60°C (140°F)
materials.action: Implement metal compression limiters (sleeves) in bolted joints or utilize Belleville spring washers to maintain tension

materials.effect: Fastener permanently seizes during installation or maintenance, requiring destructive removal
materials.cause: Friction-induced localized heat destroying the passive oxide layer during threaded engagement
materials.action: Apply anti-seize compound (molybdenum disulfide), use rolled threads instead of cut, or mix alloy grades (e.g., 304 nut on 316 bolt)

materials.effect: Optical crazing (fogging) and rapid brittle fracture propagation
materials.cause: Chemical attack from anaerobic threadlockers (Loctite), alcohol, or high installation torque
materials.action: Ban chemical threadlockers near part; specify thread-forming screws designed for plastics (PT screws)

materials.effect: Loss of dimensional tolerance and up to 30% reduction in tensile strength
materials.cause: Absorption of atmospheric moisture over time
materials.action: Design with looser tolerances or switch to moisture-resistant POM (Delrin)

materials.effect: Cracking, loss of elasticity, and sealing failure
materials.cause: UV/Ozone exposure or thermal cycling driving out plasticizers
materials.action: Verify specific elastomer compatibility with operating environment (e.g., EPDM for UV)

materials.effect: Total loss of adhesion and component detachment
materials.cause: Joint designed with cleavage/peel stresses instead of pure shear, or inadequate surface energy prep (no IPA wipe)
materials.action: Redesign joint to ensure loads are in shear/tension only; specify 50/50 IPA wipe and 15 PSI application pressure

materials.effect: Ground loop creation, electromagnetic interference, or failure to pass FCC/CE emissions testing
materials.cause: Oxidation of the conductive adhesive over time or galvanic corrosion at the grounding point
materials.action: Specify conductive acrylic adhesives and ensure mating metals are galvanically compatible (within 0.15V anodic index)

components.effect: Loss of joint clamp load and physical attachment failure
components.cause: Over-torquing in raw plastic/3D printed holes without brass inserts
components.action: Incorporate brass heat-set inserts (M3/M4) into 3D printed bosses

components.effect: Splitting or radial bursting of the mating component
components.cause: Wedge geometry of the screw head driving extreme outward radial forces into the material (highly lethal to plastics/composites)
components.action: Switch to pan head, socket head, or button head screws with flat washers to distribute load parallel to the axis

components.effect: Vibrational self-loosening and subsequent joint failure
components.cause: Re-use of the nut causing permanent plastic deformation and wear of the nylon collar
components.action: Add explicit assembly note: 'Do not reuse Nyloc nuts after initial installation', or specify deformed-thread all-metal locknuts

components.effect: Fastener backs out under vibration, or patch shreds and contaminates the assembly
components.cause: Fastener subjected to more than 3 insertion/removal cycles, destroying the nylon patch
components.action: Specify patched screws as single-use service items in maintenance manuals

components.effect: Joint loosening, rattling, or structural separation
components.cause: Oversized drill hole, or using dissimilar metals (e.g., aluminum rivet in carbon steel sheet) in humid environments
components.action: Specify exact hole tolerance (e.g., #30 drill for 1/8" rivet) and match rivet alloy to sheet metal material

components.effect: Loss of structural integrity at the bend line, breaking under load
components.cause: Bending parallel to the material grain direction, or inside bend radius being too tight for the material thickness and temper
components.action: Enforce minimum inside bend radius (e.g., 1x or 2x material thickness) and orient flat patterns 45 or 90 degrees to rolling grain

components.effect: Loss of sealing pressure resulting in fluid or pressure leak
components.cause: Thermal degradation of elastomer or gap clearance too large for operating pressure
components.action: Verify gland fill percentage (typically 70-85%) and specify backup rings if >1500psi

components.effect: Increased friction, acoustic noise, vibration, and kinematic seizure
components.cause: Lubrication starvation, particle contamination, or exceeding dynamic load rating
components.action: Specify sealed bearings (RS/ZZ) or schedule lubrication PMs

components.failure_mode: Tooth Root Bending Fatigue / Abrasive Wear
components.effect: Backlash increase, skipped teeth, or catastrophic transmission loss
components.cause: Cyclic overload, misalignment, or inadequate surface hardness
components.action: Specify case hardening (carburizing/nitriding) for gear teeth

components.effect: Loss of return force preventing mechanism reset
components.cause: Operating stresses exceeding torsional yield or cyclic fatigue limit
components.action: Shot peen springs for high-cycle applications; ensure design stays below 45% tensile strength

components.effect: Increased Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR), voltage ripple, and thermal runaway circuit failure
components.cause: Sustained operation at elevated ambient temperatures (component lifespan halves for every 10°C increase per the Arrhenius equation)
components.action: Derate operating temperature spec by 20°C, ensure PCB airflow, or switch to solid polymer/tantalum capacitors

components.effect: Exponential increase in contact resistance resulting in localized housing melt/fire
components.cause: Mechanical micro-vibrations wearing away the tin/gold plating, exposing the base copper alloy to oxidation
components.action: Apply dielectric grease, specify higher micron plating thickness, and secure wiring harnesses with strain relief within 50mm of the connector

components.effect: Short circuit to chassis, signal loss, or localized fire
components.cause: Abrasion against sharp sheet metal edges or repeated flexing exceeding minimum bend radius
components.action: Install edge grommets, route wires with service loops, and secure with zip ties every 100mm

components.effect: Intermittent electrical open circuits (especially on large BGA components)
components.cause: Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) mismatch between FR4 fiberglass and silicon components during temperature cycling
components.action: Apply conformal coating or underfill to large ICs; ensure PCB mounting includes vibration isolation standoffs

components.effect: Loss of high-frequency filtering capability, allowing EMI to pass through and failing EMC compliance
components.cause: DC bias current exceeding the ferrite core's magnetic saturation threshold
components.action: Verify peak DC operational current is well below the ferrite saturation rating; increase package size if necessary

components.effect: Short circuiting across protected components or layers
components.cause: Sharp solder tails or through-hole pins piercing the thin tape layer under compression
components.action: Apply tape with minimum 50% overlap and clip sharp through-hole leads prior to application

components.effect: Loss of torque, skipped steps, or internal short circuit
components.cause: Overheating due to sustained high current (stall condition) or restricted airflow
components.action: Implement active cooling (heatsink/fan) or software stall-detection with current rollback

components.effect: Loss of position data resulting in violent motor runaway or immediate system halt
components.cause: Ingress of dust/oil onto the optical disk, or severe shock/vibration shattering the glass encoder disk
components.action: Specify IP67 sealed encoders or switch to magnetic/resolver encoders in high-shock or dirty environments

components.effect: Load remains permanently energized (cannot turn off), risking safety hazards
components.cause: High inrush currents or inductive voltage spikes causing arcing across contacts during switching
components.action: Add a flyback diode across inductive loads and specify relays with AgSnO2 contacts for high-inrush

components.effect: Catastrophic fire, explosion, or casing rupture
components.cause: Internal short due to dendrite growth, over-discharge, or mechanical puncture
components.action: Integrate Battery Management System (BMS) with thermal cutoff, and design physical blast containment/venting enclosures

components.effect: Failure to register end-stop (machine crash) or intermittent signal bouncing
components.cause: Actuation cycles exceeding physical limit (e.g., >10^6 cycles) or low-current 'dry switching' failing to clean oxides
components.action: Use optical/inductive sensors for high-cycle end stops, or apply wetting current for mechanical switches

components.effect: Loss of safety warnings leading to operator hazard or regulatory compliance failure
components.cause: UV degradation (fading) of ink, or application to low surface energy (LSE) plastics without proper adhesive
components.action: Specify UV-resistant overlaminate and high-tack acrylic adhesives for LSE plastics like Polypropylene
